items.title: John "Knocky" Parker Interview, 1963-08-28
items.q: I think he did some subbing with Lil Waters, and Turk, and all that gang

ctx.x: The good Hillbilly musicians fit easily into any good ensemble anywhere. Swing, jazz, either one. Drag, and the, uh, that's right. And the same, the reverse also. And this is interesting too. In, uh, later, in your late period there of this Bob Wills, so often he would have swing musicians come into his group. And if they were good swim musicians, they fit well into it. That's what you're getting into those late days after I left the Do Boys. And I don't know much about this. But I do know I kept hearing about…

That's all I know. Tell them who he was. He was a trumpet player from Oklahoma, wasn't he originally? Or, I don't know. Maybe he was here. I thought he was here. No, I don't think so. Did he ever play in New Orleans? He may have. I don't know. I read something about him, and my memory is not as good as yours, and Dick Allen's. And all I know is he went out and he played with, I think he did some subbing with Lil Waters, and Turk, and all that gang. But he was maybe making a living. No, he was playing with Bob…
Yes, lots of records with Bob Wills. He fit in ideally. Yeah. That's the theory at any rate I was talking about. A good musician can do anything, and that's it.
